headline: WYOMING URANIUM MINE HALTED AFTER CYBERATTACK ON CONTROL SYSTEMS — Peninsula Energy ASX Trading Suspended Through Nov 30
snippet: Peninsula Energy's Lance uranium project in Wyoming was shut down after a cyberattack hit plant and wellfield control systems at its Strata Energy subsidiary on November 20, with the company disclosing the incident on November 25. Peninsula requested an ASX trading halt through November 30 while operations and an investigation remain suspended. The company has not named a threat actor, confirmed any data breach, or set a restart date. Peninsula had previously guided 500,000–600,000 pounds of uranium production for 2027 — that guidance is now under review and the Lance project is North America's first ISR uranium operation to be forced offline by a cyberattack.

headline: BARRICK RESTRUCTURES AHEAD OF AMERICAN BARRICK GOLD IPO — Mine Managers Get Greater Autonomy as $60B NYSE Float Nears
snippet: Barrick Gold announced it is decentralising production accountability by giving individual mine general managers greater autonomy over output targets, a structural shift tied to the pending IPO of American Barrick Gold — its North American spinoff. American Barrick Gold, which will hold Barrick's interest in Nevada Gold Mines alongside Fourmile and Pueblo Viejo, has already filed an S-1 registration with the SEC and is targeting a year-end NYSE listing under ticker ABGC at a valuation above $60 billion. Newmont consented to the IPO under an August settlement, also committing to pay Barrick US$1.95 billion, clearing the final major obstacle to the float.

headline: CONGO ON COURSE TO UNSEAT CHILE AS TOP COPPER NATION — Quarterly Exports Top 1 Million Tonnes for the First Time
snippet: The Democratic Republic of Congo posted its first-ever quarterly copper export figure above one million tonnes, closing in on Chile's long-held position as the world's dominant copper producer. The milestone reflects years of investment by Chinese mining conglomerates in Congolese copper-cobalt belts. Chile has held the top-producer title for decades, but escalating permitting delays and declining ore grades at legacy operations like Chuquicamata and Escondida have opened the door to Congo's rising output. The shift carries implications for copper supply chain security for Western manufacturers increasingly focused on non-Chinese sourcing.

headline: HARMONY GOLD BETS ON AUSTRALIAN COPPER — Targets 100,000 T/Year by 2029 as South African Gold Mines Dwindle
snippet: South Africa's Harmony Gold is pivoting toward Australian copper as attractive gold acquisition targets in its home market grow scarce, with the company's CSA mine and Eva Copper development project targeting combined annual production of 100,000 tonnes by 2029. Harmony acquired the CSA underground copper mine from Glencore in 2022 and has been advancing Eva through feasibility. The dual-track copper strategy marks a significant departure from the company's historical identity as a South African gold producer and signals where management sees superior long-run returns — particularly with South African power, water, and community permitting constraints showing no near-term relief.

headline: GDXJ STAGES BIGGEST INTRADAY REVERSAL SINCE APRIL 2020 — Silver Now Leading the Bounce as Miners Reset From Oversold Extreme
snippet: The junior gold miner ETF GDXJ closed Wednesday 10.4% above its intraday low — its most dramatic single-day reversal since April 2020 — as short sellers abandoned positions across the precious metals complex. Analysis published on InvestorIdeas notes that silver has taken the lead in percentage terms during the subsequent rally, outperforming both gold and the miners, in a pattern consistent with early-stage recoveries from oversold extremes. The piece argues the reversal is likely a corrective bounce within the medium-term decline, while flagging that silver's leadership is a historically bullish inter-market signal for the sector if sustained into December.

headline: NOVEMBER COPPER CRASH ERASED $145 BILLION FROM MAJOR MINER MARKET CAPS — Sector's Worst Month Since 2022
snippet: An 18% fall in copper prices during November 2026 wiped approximately $145 billion from the combined market capitalisation of the world's largest copper miners, the sector's worst monthly destruction of equity value since the 2022 rate-shock downturn. The selloff was driven by new U.S. tariffs, Federal Reserve rate expectations, and a cooling of AI infrastructure spending forecasts that had underpinned copper's record run above $15,000 per tonne earlier in 2026. LME copper hit a 2026 low before Friday's short-covering rally to above $12,600, leaving the technical picture uncertain heading into December.

headline: QMINES DRILLS 46.8M AT 2.29% COPPER AND 1.03 G/T GOLD BENEATH MT CHALMERS PIT (ASX: QML)
snippet: QMines (ASX: QML) returned 46.8 metres averaging 2.29% copper and 1.03 g/t gold from hole 26MCDD051 at the Mt Chalmers copper-gold project in Queensland, with a 9-metre higher-grade core inside the interval running 5.39% copper and 2.76 g/t gold. The result, from beneath the floor of the previously mined open pit, confirms high-grade copper-gold mineralisation continues at depth and expands the potential scale of the deposit ahead of an updated resource estimate. Mt Chalmers is a historic Queensland copper-gold mine that QMines relisted for a second life with modern underground drilling.

headline: BAYHORSE SILVER DRILLS 886M INTO FOUR IP TARGETS AT OREGON MINE — Underground Program Advances New Zones (TSXV: BHS)
snippet: Bayhorse Silver (TSX-V: BHS) released assay results from six underground holes totalling 886 metres, targeting four induced-polarisation anomalies identified in the company's 2025 geophysical survey at its Bayhorse silver mine in Oregon. The program is designed to test new mineralisation vectors below and adjacent to known mine workings, with the IP survey having identified four distinct targets at depth not previously drilled from underground. Bayhorse is one of a handful of TSX-V-listed silver explorers running active underground drill programs in the western U.S. amid elevated silver prices.

headline: ENTRÉE RESOURCES WARNS ON MONGOLIA LICENCE ISSUES, CONFIRMS MORE HUGO NORTH COPPER-GOLD HITS (TSX: ETG)
snippet: Entrée Resources (TSX: ETG) simultaneously updated investors on unresolved mining licence matters with Mongolian authorities and released additional drill results from the Hugo North Extension at the world-class Oyu Tolgoi deposit. The outstanding licence issues remain unresolved and could affect future project access — an ongoing risk for Entrée's minority interest in the OT underground expansion operated by Rio Tinto's Turquoise Hill. New holes confirmed continuing high-grade copper-gold mineralisation at depth in the Extension zone, adding to the geological case while the licence cloud persists.

headline: UPSIDE GOLD DRILLS 480M OF CONTINUOUS GOLD MINERALIZATION — 16 More Holes Pending (OTC: UGODF)
snippet: Upside Gold Corp (OTC: UGODF) reported a single drill hole returning a 480-metre interval of continuous gold-bearing mineralisation — one of the longest bulk-tonnage intersections reported by any junior exploration company in 2026. Full assay grades for the interval are pending, with results from an additional 16 holes in the same program also outstanding. The company described the structural continuity as a significant upgrade to its geological model. Continuous intervals of this length are uncommon in junior gold exploration and typically indicate a low-grade bulk-tonnage deposit style rather than high-grade vein mineralisation.

headline: PROSPECTIVA HITS 10M AT 11.75% COPPER AT SÃO FRANCISCO, BRAZIL — Step-Out Marks Company's Best Intersection
snippet: Prospectiva drilled step-out hole SF_26_006 at its São Francisco copper project in Brazil, cutting 10.02 metres grading 11.75% copper, 0.87 g/t gold and 1.09% zinc — the company's highest-grade copper intersection to date and one of the richest copper-only intervals reported from a Brazilian junior in recent years. The result, delivered ahead of an initial resource estimate, extends known high-grade mineralisation beyond the current drill footprint. At 11.75% copper the intersection would be economic at current prices in a small open-pit scenario, adding early-stage optionality to the project's development path.
